answer: Sequential quartz signing chain. Each agent identity must append a signed block to a shared ledger whose proof-of-work requires a physical quartz oscillator with a factory-etched serial, and the block's hash must anchor to the prior block's timing jitter within a tight tolerance. Creating a new identity costs a fresh oscillator plus the measured hours to calibrate its jitter profile against a shale reference sample. An attacker running N clones pays N oscillators and N calibration runs, and cloned profiles are detectable as correlated jitter.
